newsitem.title: POLAND: Poland's Bank Handlowy seen up after modest debut.
newsitem.headline: Poland's Bank Handlowy seen up after modest debut.

text.p: Poland's Bank Handlowy SA, which started trade on the Warsaw bourse on Monday 8.3 percent above issue at 37.9 zlotys ($11.58), should rise on Tuesday despite some profit-taking, traders said.

They said Handlowy's Monday turnover of 55.8 million zlotys, 41 percent of main-market trade, was in part accounted for by small players selling to buy copper giant KGHM Polska Miedz SA, whose public offering also started on Monday.
"I think Handlowy could have had a better debut if it had been more separated in time from the KGHM offering," one trader said.
Traders said Handlowy could approach 40 zlotys before falling back.

The 9.75-million-share retail tranche of the bank's May-June public offering at 35 zlotys each was three times subscribed and the 19.5-million-share institutional tranche was 17.4 times subscribed with foreign demand over $3.5 billion.
The 24-percent long-term investor tranche went to JP Morgan, Zurich Insurance and Swedbank .
Bank Handlowy's Global Depositary Receipts (GDRs) currently trade on the London bourse. ($ = 3.272 Polish Zlotys)
